title: Side Project Commit Drought
dataSources: GitHub repositories (`github:repo`), commits (`github:commit`), issues (`github:issue`), and releases (`github:release`).
app: GitHub repository metadata, commit activity feeds, issue trackers, and release publish logs forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=github:commit repo_name=*
| stats max(_time) as last_commit by repo_name
| eval days_since=round((now()-last_commit)/86400,0)
| where days_since>14
| sort - days_since
| table repo_name days_since
description: Flags personal repositories with no commits for more than fourteen days.
value: Commit droughts are the early signal that a side project stalled before the repo goes fully dormant.
implementation: Ingest GitHub commit webhooks per repo and alert when `days_since` exceeds your active-project threshold.
visualization: Table of repos ranked by days since last commit.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks side projects you have not touched in two weeks or more.
